clue.text: Lashings of top class cake at ball

blocks.note: A is the top grade or class, as in A1
a bun is a small cake
a ball is a formal dance; 'at' just places the cake there

explanation.surface: A generous helping of first-rate cake served at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Lashings is British informal for a great quantity, as in lashings of cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashings means plenty, a large supply, which is exactly what abundance is.

clue.text: Rite of Spring decapitated flower

indicators.note: to decapitate is to cut off the head, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: Easter is the Christian festival held in spring

explanation.surface: Stravinsky's ballet The Rite of Spring, with its sacrificial violence, seems to involve a beheaded flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R pulls you towards Stravinsky's ballet, but the phrase simply describes a spring festival.
explanation.definitionFit: An aster is a daisy-like garden plant with star-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Rebellion has no insurance priority

indicators.note: having none of something means those letters are taken away

blocks.note: an insurgency is an armed uprising
INS is a standard abbreviation of insurance

explanation.surface: Rebels who lack insurance cover have their priorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgency is the quality of demanding immediate attention, so giving something urgency is giving it priority.

clue.text: A little bit overcome by the facts

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over turns the letters upside down so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A small detail gets swamped by the facts of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome' reads as defeated, but in a down entry it means flipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are the gathered facts and figures on which reasoning rests.

clue.text: Go back on agreement to have secluded spot

indicators.note: going back means the following little word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written before being turned round
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: Someone reneges on a deal in order to keep a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back on' looks like the idiom for breaking a promise, but it splits into a reversal signal and the word on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or recess, out of the way of others.

clue.text: Choose to make a speech to voters

blocks.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A candidate opts to address the voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote.

clue.text: Rub quarter with part of sleeve

blocks.note: south, one of the four quarters of the compass
the cuff is the end part of a sleeve

explanation.surface: Wearing down a patch of fabric at the sleeve end.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuff is to scrape or graze a surface by rubbing it.

clue.text: Deer population in decline?

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer
a nation is the people of a country

explanation.surface: A wildlife survey worries that deer numbers are falling.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a stagnant state is loosely a decline: no growth, things going stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a lack of activity or growth, often in an economy, a sort of decline.

clue.text: Anonymous international organisation is aware name needed

blocks.note: the United Nations
to know is to be aware
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A global body knows a name is required, though the person stays anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unknown has no identified source, just as an anonymous author is unnamed.

clue.text: L-Laura Bush?

blocks.note: surface: someone stammering the name of the wife of US President George W. Bush
setter's reading: the opening L is the initial of the second word of the title she held, its leading letter

explanation.walkthrough: The stutter is not nerves: the lone L is the start letter of the second word of the answer, and Laura Bush held the title itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of the US President is given this title, which Laura Bush held from 2001 to 2009.

clue.text: Balancing act to make drunk leper work a shift

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: tight is informal for drunk
these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus wants an inebriated leper to work a shift as a balancing performer.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'act' here is a performer on the bill, the person who does the balancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who crosses a high wire is literally a balancing turn on the programme.

clue.text: Call round

blocks.note: first meaning: telephone someone
second meaning: a circle or circular band

explanation.walkthrough: 'Call round' reads as a visit to someone's house; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to telephone and a circular shape or band.

clue.text: Laurel expressed misgivings about project

indicators.note: expressed means spoken out, so the clue words give sounds rather than spellings

blocks.note: Stan Laurel of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy
doubt, with its silent B, is said 'dout'

explanation.surface: Stan Laurel voicing his doubts about some new scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' is the verb, to jut out, not the noun for a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to protrude beyond a surface, just as a ledge projects from a wall.

clue.text: Dashing fellow and son between them beat a knight at last

indicators.note: placing something between two others means it sits inside the pair
last points to the final letter of the little word at

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
to lam is to thrash
a son is a boy
taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight
the final letter of at

explanation.surface: A dashing chap and his son together defeat a knight in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant describes showy, confident style, the same flair a dashing person has.

clue.text: White stars transformed sports top

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A team's white star badge has been redesigned on its kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshirt is a loose cotton jersey worn for sport or exercise.

clue.text: A fly mashed in grass cutter: a harbinger of summer?

indicators.note: mashed means crushed to a pulp, so these letters are jumbled
in places the jumbled letters inside the next item

blocks.note: these four letters rearranged
a lawnmower cuts grass

explanation.surface: An insect gets chewed up in the lawnmower as warm weather arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayflower is the hawthorn, whose May blossom heralds summer; the question mark marks this as a description, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blossom opens in May, so its appearance signals that summer is on its way.

clue.text: Has doubts about girl holding responsibility

indicators.note: holding means wrapping round, so one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman
a trust is a duty or charge placed on someone

explanation.surface: Someone is uneasy about a young woman given a position of responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to be suspicious of or lack confidence in someone.

clue.text: Hundred grand gets last villa on Friendly Islands

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
the final letter of villa

explanation.surface: A hundred thousand buys the last villa in a South Pacific holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook named the islands the Friendly Islands after his warm welcome there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific kingdom was nicknamed the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook in 1773.

clue.text: Go away with S. Coe's old rival

blocks.note: taken as written
Steve Cram, the British middle-distance runner who raced against Sebastian Coe in the 1980s

explanation.surface: Telling someone to be off while naming Sebastian Coe's great rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe and Steve Cram were rival British middle-distance runners of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a curt informal command to leave at once.

clue.text: Little girl won at gymkhana?

blocks.note: surface: a young girl took first place at a pony show
setter's reading: the diminutive suffix -ette on a flower name makes a little girl's name, and the result is the ribbon prize handed out at pony shows

explanation.walkthrough: A gymkhana is a children's horse-riding competition, where winners get a ribbon badge; read 'little Rose' to find the prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is the circular ribbon badge awarded to placed riders at a gymkhana.

clue.text: Worker gets spiritual about Passover collection

indicators.note: over means turned round, so the short word before it is read backwards
about means surrounding, so one part wraps round the other

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker
holy means sacred or spiritual
the first part, pass, gives go, as in time going by; the tail of the word is the reversal signal

explanation.surface: A labourer acquires a religious book about the Jewish festival of Passover.
explanation.walkthrough: Passover looks like one word naming the festival; split it into a verb and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a collection of poems or stories gathered in one book.

clue.text: Always busy, won't he goof about a bit?

indicators.note: a bit means only a part, so the letters sit inside a longer run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across the first three words

explanation.surface: A busy person asks whether he'll ever fool around a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the go means constantly active, never resting.

clue.text: Reply to awkward person on small point

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: these six letters rearranged
S is the abbreviation for small
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Answering a difficult individual on some minor issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward person' looks like one description, but awkward is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is an answer to a question or message.

clue.text: Find it finally in plant store

indicators.note: finally points to the very end letter of the phrase before it
in places one item inside the next

blocks.note: the final letter of the phrase
to sow is to plant seed

explanation.surface: Instructions to locate something at last in a garden centre or factory store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a factory or greenery; here it is the verb, to put seed in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack something away for keeping, to store it.

clue.text: Got back en route before Rooney comes

indicators.note: getting back means going in the opposite direction, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: a way is a route; 'before' puts it first
taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: Someone returned while travelling, just before the footballer arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Rooney is England's former football captain and record goalscorer; the definition is by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooney's first name is the answer, so the surname points to the footballer and thus his given name.

clue.text: King has no time to bond

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written; has just joins
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A busy monarch can't spare the time to form a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a tie that fastens, and a tie or link is a bond.

clue.text: Weaver uses this family property, there being no beneficiary

indicators.note: with none of something present, those letters are taken out

blocks.note: an heirloom is a treasured possession handed down in a family
an heir is someone who inherits

explanation.surface: A weaver works with an inherited family piece, as nobody else stands to inherit it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the wordplay: 'uses this' turns the weaver into a pointer at the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A loom is the frame or machine on which a weaver interlaces threads into cloth.

clue.text: TV programme location seemingly modest when male editor dropped in

indicators.note: dropped in means placed inside, so these letters go into the middle of another word

blocks.note: a situation is a site or position
coy means affecting shyness, appearing modest
M is the abbreviation for male
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A TV show's set looks unassuming once a man from the editing room drops by.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy, or sitcom, is a television series of humorous episodes about the same characters.

clue.text: Street has oddly clean smell

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in the odd positions, first, third and fifth
to have something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
letters one, three and five of clean

explanation.surface: An odd street that smells unusually clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a distinctive smell, especially a pleasant one.

clue.text: The heartless politician's come into ill-gotten gains backing key tribal art

indicators.note: without a heart, the middle letter is dropped
coming into means entering, so these letters go inside the next item
backing means moving backwards, so the word before it is read in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its middle
MP, Member of Parliament
loot is stolen goods
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A cynical politician cashes in on plunder, sponsoring key tribal artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: The heartless word is THE with its middle H gone; the reversed plunder wraps round that pair, and the key comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a carved and painted post made by peoples of the Pacific Northwest, a famous form of tribal art.
